trust_decision.summary: How much inbound text a gateway peer may make the client accumulate for one multi-frame WebSocket message; decided (absent) in the shared receive loop of WebSocketClientBase, which appends every non-final frame to a StringBuilder with no total cap.

landing_point.why: A 'DoS / unbounded allocation in the gateway transport' summary leads straight to the only ClientWebSocket.ReceiveAsync loop in the tree and its sb.Append.

fix_sites.entry_point: Gateway WebSocket inbound text messages to the node client (WindowsNodeClient, src/OpenClaw.Shared/WindowsNodeClient.cs:17) and to the operator client (OpenClawGatewayClient, src/OpenClaw.Shared/OpenClawGatewayClient.cs:15), both via the inherited ListenForMessagesAsync
New internal helper TryAppendWithinLimit + MaxInboundMessageChars constant, called only from the same receive loop

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: Both clients inherit one loop (src/OpenClaw.Shared/WindowsNodeClient.cs:114, src/OpenClaw.Shared/OpenClawGatewayClient.cs:155 only set ReceiveBufferSize); no second WebSocket receive implementation exists in src/ (only ReceiveAsync call is src/OpenClaw.Shared/WebSocketClientBase.cs:228).

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Nothing to dismiss: the single shared loop is the only route; the only arguable gap is the single-frame fast path (src/OpenClaw.Shared/WebSocketClientBase.cs:237-240), which is already bounded by the receive buffer size.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Large legitimate multi-frame gateway messages (e.g. base64 attachments) must still be reassembled and delivered; the fix picks a generous 32M-char cap and the test bounds it to 8M..128M chars. A too-small cap, or capping per frame/at the fast path, would break them.

O6_input_shapes: Multi-frame text message that never sets EndOfMessage (unbounded continuation frames)
Multi-frame text message whose reassembled total exceeds the cap even though it does end

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A binary-message reassembly branch (WebSocketMessageType.Binary appended to a MemoryStream) without the cap, e.g. for attachment or audio frames.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The loop currently only branches on Text and Close; a maintainer adding binary support for attachments would plausibly copy the multi-frame pattern into a second buffer.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: An operator-client override of the receive loop (or a dedicated chat-stream socket in another package) that re-implements frame reassembly.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Subclasses already customise ReceiveBufferSize per role; a separate streaming client for chat would be a plausible second implementation at distance.

O9_family: CWE-770 unbounded allocation: inbound WebSocket multi-frame message accumulation with no total cap

O10_build.toolchain: dotnet SDK 10 (net10.0, src/OpenClaw.Shared/OpenClaw.Shared.csproj:4); OpenClaw.Shared is a plain library, the Tray project is WinUI (Windows-only)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Check sb.Length before sb.Append in the multi-frame branch and close the socket on overflow, which is essentially the published fix.

out_of_scope_notes: Fix commit 4206611f (fix.diff:1-928) is an unrelated MXC sandbox feature (Allow Windows UI APIs / PowerShell direct-argv UI check), not CWE-770.

browser.proxy reads the local browser-control HTTP response with ReadAsStringAsync on a default HttpClient with no explicit body cap (src/OpenClaw.Shared/Capabilities/BrowserProxyCapability.cs:47, :77, :84); this is a different sink and was not pursued.

Other inbound readers are already bounded: MCP HTTP body (src/OpenClaw.Shared/Mcp/McpHttpServer.cs:369-391), deep-link IPC pipe (src/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI/App.xaml.cs:4355-4382), A2UI image fetch (src/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI/A2UI/Rendering/MediaResolver.cs:240-275).
